1use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::reader::Reader;
2use alloc::vec;
3use alloc::vec::Vec;
4
5/// PdfCraft patch: `limit` is the most bytes produced (see `filter::decode_limit`); a run of 128
6/// copies costs two input bytes, so a few megabytes could ask for gigabytes.
7pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
8    let mut reader = Reader::new(data);
9    let mut decoded = vec![];
10
11    loop {
12        let left = limit.saturating_sub(decoded.len());
13        if left == 0 {
14            break;
15        }
16        let length = reader.read_byte()?;
17
18        match length {
19            128 => break,
20            0..=127 => {
21                // PDFBOX-3990, just abort early if stream is invalid.
22                let Some(bytes) = reader.read_bytes(length as usize + 1) else {
23                    break;
24                };
25
26                decoded.extend(bytes.iter().take(left));
27            }
28            _ => {
29                let length = (257 - length as usize).min(left);
30                let byte = reader.read_byte()?;
31                decoded.extend(core::iter::repeat_n(byte, length));
32            }
33        }
34    }
35
36    // PdfCraft patch: output cut at the limit is reported, never dropped silently.
37    if decoded.len() >= limit {
38        warn!("run-length stream stopped at its decode limit of {limit} bytes");
39    }
40    Some(decoded)
41}
